description: Logistics Capacity Assessments are country profiles of logistics infrastructure prepared by the World Food Programme for the humanitarian Logistics Cluster, now published as a digital site. The index read on 2026-09-28 lists about 140 country assessments, from Afghanistan to Zimbabwe, including limited port assessments for some countries such as Argentina, Brazil and Mexico, limited assessments for others, and entries for Hungary, Poland and Romania prepared for the Ukraine response; the site is offered in seven languages. The country pages refused the cloud session, so which infrastructure each assessment covers, such as ports, roads or storage, was not read here and should be checked before use. A disclaimer notes that assessments name companies only to indicate services and capacities. Coverage is global, weighted to countries with humanitarian operations. Access to the web pages is free; no licence is stated on the index. Caveats: currency varies by country, the contents per country were not read, and the assessments are narrative with tables, not structured data. It supports emergency response and resilience studies, such as comparing port and warehouse capacity along relief corridors before a cyclone season. Related records: WFP's SDI-T logistics layers and roads service.
